finding: On Windows, a busy swap that creates a new file is now refused at once as 'is read-only' instead of being retried, because os.access returns False for a path that does not exist.
why: Scenario: update_locked on a missing file (the docstring says a missing file reads as "", and install_block._update reaches it when a user instruction file does not exist yet); another process (scanner, indexer) holds the fresh temp file, so os.replace raises PermissionError; os.access(write_target, os.W_OK) on the missing write_target returns False (probed here: os.access on a nonexistent path -> False), so the SDD §7 retry row ('file swap busy on Windows | 10 retries at 50 ms') is skipped and setup fails with the wrong cause. Every busy-swap test (test_safe_write.py:158-205) uses an existing target, so none catches it.
fix: Treat only an existing file as read-only, e.g. `if write_target.exists() and not os.access(write_target, os.W_OK)` (or stat it and check the read-only bit, FileNotFoundError meaning not read-only); add a busy_replace test on a missing target that expects 11 calls and a written file.
evidence:
